title: Does reflectivity help?
blurb: PointNet and PointNet++, with and without the reflectivity channel, plus seed repeats that show how big a meaningless difference looks.

arms.label: PointNet · shape only
arms.what: PointNet with the reflectivity channel removed entirely. The control: whatever this scores is what pure geometry is worth.

arms.label: PointNet · shape + reflectivity
arms.what: PointNet with reflectivity included, using the standard augmentation (reflectivity randomly rescaled and shifted each sample). This is the setting the existing runs used.

arms.label: PointNet++ · shape only
arms.what: PointNet++ with no reflectivity. The shape-only control for the hierarchical model.

arms.label: PointNet++ · shape + reflectivity
arms.what: PointNet++ with reflectivity included and the standard augmentation.

arms.label: PointNet · reflectivity unjittered
arms.what: PointNet with reflectivity included and the reflectivity augmentation switched off, so the model may use the raw absolute brightness. If reflectivity helps anywhere, it helps most here — and the gap between this and the jittered arm is the size of the cue the augmentation deliberately destroys.

arms.label: PointNet++ · reflectivity unjittered
arms.what: PointNet++ with reflectivity included and its augmentation off.

arms.label: PointNet · reflectivity only
arms.what: PointNet fed nothing but reflectivity — no coordinates at all. It cannot see shape, so its score is a direct read of how much the brightness numbers alone can separate rock from sand.

arms.label: PointNet · shape only (seed 43)
arms.what: Same setting as the shape-only arm, different random seed. Exists only to measure how far two identical settings land apart.

arms.label: PointNet · shape + reflectivity (seed 43)
arms.what: Seed repeat of the shape+reflectivity arm.

arms.label: PointNet · shape only (seed 44)
arms.what: Second seed repeat of the shape-only arm.

arms.label: PointNet · shape + reflectivity (seed 44)
arms.what: Second seed repeat of the shape+reflectivity arm.
